text: neocord is a framework for Discord bots. You write commands, buttons, selects, modals, events and tasks as files, return JSX from handlers, and neocord handles dispatch, replies, command deploys and sharding. It is built on discord.js and React, and runs on Bun and on Node. The neocord command needs Node 22.22 or later if you run it with Node, and the runtime packages need Node 22.12 or later.

heading: Why neocord
text: A discord.js bot usually starts with a registry of handlers, a switch on customId , a script to deploy commands, and a message builder for every reply. neocord replaces each of those with a convention: The file path is the route. commands/ping/command.tsx is /ping , and buttons/refresh/button.tsx handles the button whose custom id is general/refresh . There is nothing to register. JSX is the message. @teamneo/neocord-react is a real React renderer. Function components, context, hooks and <Suspense> work, the output is Discord's Components V2 JSON, and Discord's limits are checked at render time. Routes are typed. The CLI generates types from your files, so <Button route="general/refresh" />

heading: Rules that follow from this
text: Slash commands are global. The feature is not part of the name, so /ban can only exist once across all features. Each interaction type has its own route table. A button and a modal can share the id moderation/ban-reason/[userId] . Static segments win. When matching a custom id, a static segment beats a [param] , and a [param] beats a [...rest] . Ids starting with ~ are reserved for live sessions . Custom ids have a 100 character limit. Building a longer one throws. See Dynamic routes .

heading: How a project is checked
text: Problems are reported at two levels. scanProject in the CLI reads the file tree and reports these before anything runs: Files with the wrong name, in an unknown folder, or directly in the features folder. Two routes with the same id and kind. Events are exempt, because several files can listen to one event. Two dynamic routes in the same place with different param names, such as [id] and [userId] . Commands deeper than three levels, invalid command names, and a command that also has subcommands. Two middleware , layout , error or loading files in one folder. validateManifest loads the modules and checks what they export. It reports errors for wrong helpers, route literals that do not match t

heading: Dispatch
text: When an interaction arrives, neocord: Finds the route. If nothing matches, it logs a warning and replies ephemerally with "This interaction is no longer available." Resolves the guild and member. With guildOnly , it fetches them if they are missing and replies with a notice if there are none. Checks permissions against the member's permissions. Builds the context, including parsed options, params or modal values. Runs the middleware chain from root to leaf. Applies the cooldown , sends loading.tsx for commands, and runs your handler. Delivers what the handler returned. See Replying . If anything throws, the closest error view is shown ephemerally and the error is logged.

A feature is a folder in src/features . It groups the commands, buttons, selects, modals, events and tasks that belong together, and gives them a shared set of middleware, layouts and error views. A folder becomes a feature as soon as it holds a route or a segment file. It does not need a feature.ts .

heading: defineFeature
text: Add a feature.ts to configure a feature. Its default export must be defineFeature : Field Type Default Meaning enabled boolean true When false , the feature contributes no commands, routes, events, tasks, intents or partials. intents Keys of GatewayIntentBits None Merged with intents from neocord.config.ts , which defaults to ["Guilds"] . partials Keys of Partials None Merged with partials from neocord.config.ts . defineFeature() with no argument is also valid. The type of enabled is boolean . If SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION leaves a raw string in its place, the strings false , 0 , no , off , n and disabled still disable the feature, in any case.

heading: Intents belong with the code that needs them
text: If only one feature listens to messageCreate , ask for the intent in that feature rather than in the config. Disable the feature and the intent goes with it: MessageContent , GuildMembers and GuildPresences are privileged, so they must also be enabled in the Discord Developer Portal. Otherwise Discord closes the connection with code 4014. See Troubleshooting .

heading: Disabling a feature
text: A disabled feature's routes are removed from the manifest before validation, command serialisation and dispatch. Its commands are not deployed, and neocord does not listen for its events or run its tasks. / Note The generated manifest still imports every file statically, so the bundler sees every route. Code at the top level of a disabled feature's files still runs when the bot starts. Put work such as opening connections in a handler or in src/context.ts . If you disable a feature that sends messages with buttons, clicks on old messages reach no route. The user gets the ephemeral notice "This interaction is no longer available."

heading: Scoped files
text: A feature can have its own middleware.ts , layout.tsx , error.tsx and loading.tsx , which apply to everything inside it. They run after, or override, the ones in src : See Middleware , Layouts , Error boundaries and Loading UI .

heading: Private code
text: Folders and files starting with _ are never routed, at any depth. Use them for components and helpers: Any other unexpected file in a feature is an error, which keeps a typo in a folder name from silently producing no route.

heading: Names across features
text: Interaction routes include the feature name, so moderation/confirm and fun/confirm do not collide. Slash commands do not include it, so two features cannot both define /ban . Events are not unique either, and several features can listen to guildMemberAdd . Tasks include the feature name. Two features can contribute to one command tree. moderation/commands/mod/warn and admin/commands/mod/kick both become subcommands of /mod . One group file for /mod must exist, in either feature.
A slash command is a command.tsx file in a folder under commands . The folder names are the command's name, and the file's default export is defineCommand .

heading: Names
text: Command names must be lowercase, 1-32 characters, using letters, numbers, - , _ or ' . Each level of a nested command follows the same rule. Slash commands are global, so names must be unique across features.

heading: permissions and guildOnly
text: Both deploy to Discord, so the client hides the command, and both are also enforced at runtime. Situation What the user sees guildOnly route used outside a server "This can only be used in a server." permissions route used without a member "This can only be used in a server." Missing permissions "You need these permissions to do that: Ban Members." All of these are ephemeral, and the handler does not run. you used /ban / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 You need these permissions to do that: Ban Members. Only you can see this message

heading: cooldown
text: cooldown is a duration , and is tracked per user and route, in memory, per process. If the user is on cooldown, they get an ephemeral message with a relative timestamp and the handler does not run. Middleware denials do not consume a cooldown, because the check runs after middleware.

heading: Subcommands
text: Discord does not allow a command to be both runnable and a parent, so a folder holds either a command file or nested commands. Add a group.ts next to the subcommands to give the parent its description: These are /mod warn and /mod kick . The group's permissions and guildOnly apply to every subcommand under it at runtime, merged with any set on the subcommand. / Note guildOnly on a group does not change the subcommand's types, so ctx.guild is still nullable there. To make it non-null, also set guildOnly: true on the subcommand. validateManifest only warns about guildOnly on a subcommand when its root group does not set it, so this produces no warning.

heading: Subcommand groups
text: Add one more level for /mod case view . Every parent needs a group file, because Discord requires a description at each level: Commands can be at most three levels deep, so a group cannot be three levels deep. A root command can hold subcommands and subcommand groups at the same time.

heading: defineGroup
text: Field Type Required Meaning description string Yes 1-100 characters. permissions PermissionsString[] No Deployed on a top-level group. guildOnly boolean No Deployed on a top-level group. nsfw boolean No Deployed on a top-level group. nameLocalizations LocalizationMap No Localised names. descriptionLocalizations LocalizationMap No Localised descriptions.

heading: Where permissions live
text: Discord only stores permissions , guildOnly and nsfw on top-level commands. On a plain command like /ban , they deploy from defineCommand . On a command with subcommands, they deploy from the group.ts in its root folder. On a subcommand, permissions and guildOnly are enforced at runtime only. validateManifest warns about this and tells you to use defineGroup . On a nested group, permissions and guildOnly are enforced at runtime only. validateManifest warns about this and tells you to set them on the top-level group. nsfw has no runtime check, so on a subcommand or a nested group it is ignored. validateManifest warns about both. Set it on the top-level group instead.

heading: Organising commands
text: Route group folders in parentheses do not change the name: This is still /mod warn , and the middleware.ts applies only to what is inside (staff) .

heading: What gets deployed
text: serializeCommands turns your files into the JSON Discord expects. Run neocord deploy --dry-run to see the command tree without calling Discord. neocord dev syncs to your development server automatically, and production needs neocord deploy .

Options are declared in the options object of defineCommand . Each key is the option's name, each value comes from an option.* helper, and ctx.options is typed from them with no code generation. you used /roll / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 Initiative: 17 ctx.options.sides is 6 | 20 , and ctx.options.label is string | undefined .

Required options are sorted first when commands are serialised, because Discord requires that order. You can declare them in any order. Option names must be lowercase, 1-32 characters, using letters, numbers, - , _ or ' .

heading: Choices
text: Strings, integers and numbers accept choices . The values become a literal union, without as const : ctx.options.size is "s" | "l" | undefined . An option needs 1-25 choices, each choice name is 1-100 characters, and a string choice value is 1-100 characters. choices and autocomplete are mutually exclusive. The types forbid using both, and validateManifest reports it as an error.

heading: Autocomplete
text: For strings, integers and numbers, autocomplete is a function that returns choices as the user types: The value's type stays string or number , because Discord does not stop a user sending something that was not suggested. Check it in execute if that matters.

heading: The autocomplete context
text: Field Type Meaning focused string What the user has typed so far. optionName string The option being completed. interaction AutocompleteInteraction The raw interaction. guild Guild | null The server. member GuildMember | null The member. user User The user. client , app , logger , feature , route , shards , commands As on every context . The handler may be async and returns at most 25 choices. neocord cuts off anything after that. If it throws, the error is logged and Discord gets an empty list. guildOnly and permissions of the command are checked first. A user who fails them gets an empty list, the handler does not run, and no message is sent. Autocomplete does not run middleware or cooldow

heading: Channels
text: channelTypes limits which channels Discord offers, and narrows the value's type: ctx.options.channel is a text channel, so send is available without a type check.

heading: user and member
text: Both deploy as a Discord user option. The difference is what you get back. option.user gives a User , which always exists. option.member gives a GuildMember . neocord fetches the member if the interaction did not include one. Discord can only guarantee the user. If a required member option names someone who has left the server, neocord replies ephemerally with The user given for "name" is not a member of this server. and does not run the handler. An optional one is undefined . If any other required option cannot be resolved, the reply is The "name" option could not be resolved.

Context menu commands appear when someone right-clicks a user or a message. A user command is a command.tsx in a folder under user-commands , and a message command is a command.tsx in a folder under message-commands .

heading: User commands
text: you used Report user / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 Reported ada. Only you can see this message Context field Type Meaning target User The user who was clicked. targetMember GuildMember | null Their member. It is null when the interaction carries no member, such as for a user who has left the server, even with guildOnly: true .

heading: Message commands
text: you used Quote message / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 Ship it on Friday. Context field Type Meaning target Message The message that was clicked. Both contexts have everything in the handler context as well.

heading: Fields
text: defineUserCommand and defineMessageCommand take the same fields. Field Type Required Meaning name string Yes The name in Discord's menu, 1-32 characters. execute (ctx) => node | void Yes The handler. permissions PermissionsString[] No Hides it from members without them, and is checked at runtime. guildOnly boolean No Only usable in servers. heading: Names come from the field
text: Unlike slash commands, the name field is what Discord shows, and it can contain capitals and spaces. The folder name only sets the route id, such as moderation/report , and is not checked as a Discord name. neocord dispatches these commands by name , so two user commands cannot have the same name, and neither can two message commands. A user command and a message command may share a name.

heading: Replying
text: Context menu commands reply the same way as slash commands. Return a node, or call ctx.reply . If a handler returns nothing and has not acknowledged, neocord logs a warning. See Replying . A context menu command can also open a modal, which must be the first response: See Modals .

heading: Limits
text: Discord allows 15 user commands and 15 message commands. Both limits are checked by validateManifest . They deploy with your slash commands through neocord deploy , and neocord deploy --dry-run lists them as Report user (user) and Quote message (message) .
A button has two halves: the <Button> in a message, and the button.tsx file that runs when someone clicks it. The route prop connects them.

heading: A button and its handler
text: Send the button from any handler: Then handle it. The first argument must be the file's route id: you used /ban / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 Ban ada? Ban

Defaults to "update" . permissions PermissionsString[] No Checked at runtime against the member who clicked. guildOnly boolean No Rejects clicks outside a server. Makes ctx.guild and ctx.member non-null. ephemeral boolean No Replies from this handler are ephemeral by default. cooldown Duration No Per user and route. layout boolean No false skips layouts.

Promise<void> Updates the message. deferUpdate() Promise<void> Acknowledges and keeps the message as it is.

heading: update or reply
text: By default, a returned node replaces the message the button is on, which is what you want for a counter or a confirmation: Set respond: "reply" to send a new message instead: respond also sets what autoDefer does if the handler is slow. With "update" it defers the update, so Discord shows no loading message. With "reply" it defers a new reply.

heading: Returning nothing
text: If a button handler returns nothing and has not acknowledged, neocord calls deferUpdate , so the user does not see "This interaction failed". Do your work and return: See Replying for the full rules.

heading: Opening a modal
text: A modal must be the first response to an interaction, so call showModal before anything slow: See Modals .

heading: Who can click
text: Anyone who can see a message can click its buttons. permissions and guildOnly on defineButton are checked at runtime when the button is clicked. Unlike commands, nothing is deployed to Discord, so the button still appears for everyone. To limit it to one person, put their id in a param and compare it:

heading: Other ways to address a button
text: <Button> takes one of three addresses, and the types keep them mutually exclusive: Prop Use it for route and params A handler file. This is the preferred form, and it is type-checked. customId A raw id. The ESLint rule prefer-route-prop warns about literals. onClick A handler in the component, which needs a live session . Link buttons use style="link" and url , and premium buttons use style="premium" and skuId . They have no handler. See Interactive components for every prop. A click that matches no route gets the ephemeral notice "This interaction is no longer available." and a warning in your logs.

A modal is a modal.tsx file that defines both the form and what happens when it is submitted. Open it from another handler with ctx.showModal .

heading: A modal

With a schema , it only accepts the schema's keys, so a typo is a compile error. render is synchronous, and a suspending component throws. Layouts do not apply to modals. A modal holds 1-5 Label or TextDisplay children, and each Label wraps one control. Text can sit directly in the form, and a fragment can return several children. See Modal components for every control.

heading: showModal
text: ctx.showModal(route, params) is available on commands, context menus, buttons and selects. Modal submit , autocomplete, events and tasks do not have it. route is typed from your modal files, and params is required exactly when the route has params. It must be the first response. If the interaction has already been acknowledged, it throws an error that says so. A loading.tsx that applies to the route sends a reply first, so showModal cannot follow it. A modal cannot open from a modal submit.

Checkbox boolean Read uploaded files with ctx.fields.getUploadedFiles(name) .

It runs before cooldown , so a failed parse does not use up the cooldown. TextInput values are omitted when left blank, so use .optional() for a field the user can skip. If parsing fails, submit does not run, and the user gets an ephemeral message with the issues: / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 Please check your answers: - reason: Too small: expected string to have at least 3 characters. Set after middleware, so only submit can read them. fields ModalSubmitFields The discord.js fields, for uploaded files and raw access. update(node, options?) heading: Updating the message the modal came from
text: When a button opens a modal, respond: "update" makes the submission change the message that button is on instead of sending a new one. This suits a confirmation flow, where the buttons should disappear once the form is sent. A modal opened from a slash command has no message to update. There, respond: "update" and ctx.update send a reply, and ctx.deferUpdate defers one. See Replying .

Buttons, selects and modals can carry data in their custom id. A folder named [param] makes that part of the route dynamic, and neocord builds and parses the id for you with full types.

heading: Catch-all params
text: [...rest] catches every remaining segment and gives you an array. It must be the last segment: ctx.params.path is a string[] . A route ending in [...rest] needs at least one value.

It registers every button, select and modal route with @teamneo/neocord-react : So this is what the compiler checks: Code Result <Button route="general/refresh" label="Go" /> Compiles. <Button route="general/refrsh" label="Go" /> Error, no such route. <Button route="moderation/confirm-ban/[userId]" label="Go" /> Error, params is required. <Button route="general/refresh" params={{ id: 1 }} label="Go" /> Error, this route has no params. heading: How custom ids are built
text: buildCustomId fills in the route and encodes each value with encodeURIComponent : This returns moderation/confirm-ban/123 . A value with a slash in it stays one segment, because the slash is encoded. It throws a CustomIdError when: A param has no value, or the value is empty. A catch-all param is not a non-empty array. The result is longer than 100 characters, which is Discord's limit. / Warning Everything in a custom id counts towards the 100 characters, after encoding. Keep route names short, and store large data elsewhere with an id in the route. validateManifest reports a route whose static part alone is over the limit, but a long param value only fails when the component renders. heading: How custom ids are matched
text: Each kind has its own router, so a button and a modal can have the same id. When an interaction arrives, segments are compared left to right, in this order: A static segment. A [param] . A [...rest] . So with these two buttons, moderation/confirm/all matches the first: Values are decoded before they reach ctx.params . If nothing matches, or a value cannot be decoded, the user gets the ephemeral notice "This interaction is no longer available."

heading: A raw customId

A file in events listens to a discord.js client event. The file or folder name is the event's name, and the default export is defineEvent . The arguments after ctx are the ones discord.js passes for that event, fully typed.

heading: Files
text: Use either form: The folder form lets one event have several listeners, in one feature or across features. Each one runs separately. Nesting deeper than one folder is an error. Segment file names have no special meaning here, because every file in events is a route. events/error.ts listens to the error event.

heading: defineEvent
text: Field Type Required Meaning execute (ctx, ...args) => unknown Yes The listener. May be async. once boolean No Uses client.once instead of client.on . The first argument must be a string literal equal to the name from the path. The runtime rejects a mismatch, and the ESLint rules route-matches-path and valid-event-name catch it earlier, along with names that are not real client events. The bot's ready event in discord.js 14 is clientReady :

heading: The event context

See Listing commands . execute returns no UI. Middleware, layouts, error.tsx and loading.tsx do not apply to events. To send a message, use discord.js directly. @teamneo/neocord-react still renders the payload, and send needs the flags replaced, because it does not accept the ephemeral flag:

text: If execute throws or rejects, the error is logged with the event and file, and the process keeps running.

text: Discord only sends an event if you ask for its intent. Add it to intents in neocord.config.ts , or to defineFeature in the feature that needs it: validateManifest warns when an event's intent is not enabled, and also warns about reading message content without MessageContent . heading: Sharding
text: Each shard has its own client, so a listener runs once per shard that receives the event. See Sharding .

heading: Testing
text: runEvent resolves to { error } , because event errors never throw. See Testing .
A file in tasks runs code on an interval. The file or folder name is the task's name, and the default export is defineTask .

heading: Files
text: Use either form. The route id is moderation/cleanup , so these two would collide and neocord reports an error. Task ids must be unique, though two features can each have a cleanup . Unlike events, a folder holds only one task, and nesting deeper is an error.

heading: defineTask
text: Field Type Required Default Meaning every Duration Yes How often to run. execute (ctx) => unknown Yes The work. May be async. runOnStart boolean No false Also run once as soon as the client is ready. shard "first" | "all" No "first" "first" runs only on the shard that holds shard 0. "all" runs on every shard.

heading: Durations
text: every and cooldown take a duration, which is a number of milliseconds or a string: Input Milliseconds 500 500 "500ms" 500 "5s" 5000 "5m" 300000 "1h30m" 5400000 "1d" 86400000 The units are ms , s , m , h and d . parseDuration , exported from neocord , does the conversion and throws on anything else. every must be between 1 millisecond and 2147483647 milliseconds, which is about 24.8 days. Anything outside that is a validation error, because it is the longest delay a timer supports.

heading: When tasks run
text: Tasks start on clientReady . The first interval begins then, so a task with every: "5m" first runs five minutes later, unless runOnStart is true . If a run is still going when the next one is due, the next one is skipped, so runs never overlap. The interval does not keep the process alive. On shutdown, intervals stop, and neocord waits up to five seconds for running tasks to finish.

heading: The task context
text: Task contexts have the same fields as event contexts : client , app , logger , feature , route , shards and commands . Middleware, layouts, error.tsx and loading.tsx do not apply.

heading: Errors
text: If execute throws or rejects, the error is logged with the task and file. The process keeps running, and the task runs again at the next interval.

heading: Sharding
text: With the default shard: "first" , a task runs once however many shards you have, which suits work like cleaning a database. With no sharding manager, it always runs. Use shard: "all" for work that only touches what each shard holds, such as its cached guilds: To read across all shards from a "first" task, use ctx.shards : See Sharding . / Note Tasks live in memory and restart with the process, so every counts from the last start. Run scheduled jobs that must not be missed from an external scheduler or from a database record.

heading: Testing
text: runTask runs the task once and resolves to { error } . See Testing .

heading: Reading the context from a component
text: useContext() from neocord returns the current interaction context from any component rendered by neocord. It throws when used elsewhere. The default return type is AnyContext , and you can name a narrower one. This is useContext from neocord , not the one from react . React's still works for your own React contexts. See Custom components .

heading: Checks before the handler
text: neocord runs these steps in order for commands, context menus, buttons, selects and modals: Resolve guild and member , and enforce guildOnly . Enforce permissions against interaction.memberPermissions . A missing permission gets an ephemeral list of what is missing. Start the autoDefer timer. Build the context. This resolves options. Run middleware , root to leaf. Parse the modal schema, for modals only. A failed parse replies with the issues and stops here. Apply cooldown . text: Pass kinds to run only on some route kinds. ctx narrows to match, so ctx.options is available when kinds is ["command"] . The available kinds are "command" , "user-command" , "message-command" , "button" , "select" and "modal" .

heading: Sharing values
text: ctx.state is a new object for each interaction. Middleware can write to it and later middleware or the handler can read it. Values are unknown , so cast or check them when you read them. Use src/context.ts for services that live as long as the process.

heading: Ordering with other checks
text: guildOnly and permissions run before middleware. A modal's schema , cooldown and loading.tsx run after it, so a request denied by middleware does not parse the form, does not consume a cooldown and does not send a loading message. The full order is on the handler context page.

A layout is a plain React component that wraps the output of the handlers beneath it. Put a layout.tsx in a folder and default-export the component. It receives children and returns host components. A handler that returns <TextDisplay>Banned.</TextDisplay> now sends that text with the subtext below it. you used /ban / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 Banned. Moderation actions are logged.

heading: Composition
text: Layouts compose from root to leaf. The first layout in the chain is the outermost, so for a route under src/features/moderation : Unlike error and loading , all layouts in the chain apply. Only one layout is allowed per folder.

heading: What layouts wrap
text: Layouts wrap every node that goes through ctx.reply , ctx.editReply , ctx.followUp , ctx.update or a return value, as well as loading.tsx . They also wrap live sessions , so hooks inside a layout stay mounted with the session. They do not apply to: Modals. Error views . Cooldown, permission and validation notices from neocord. Events and tasks.

heading: Opting out
text: Set layout: false on the route, or pass it per call. A value in the call wins over the route.

heading: Layouts and Message
text: When a handler returns a <Message> element, neocord keeps it at the root and applies layouts inside it. ephemeral and allowedMentions are preserved: neocord only looks at the returned element itself. If your own component renders <Message> and a layout applies, the Message ends up inside the layout and the render throws "Message must be the root of the tree." Return <Message> directly from the handler, or set ephemeral on the route.

heading: Watch the nesting

A Container cannot hold another Container , so a layout that wraps children in a Container fails on any handler that also returns one: The error is "Container is not allowed inside Container." Fragments avoid this, as in the first example. The layout components page lists what each component can hold.

heading: How it is delivered
text: The view is sent with ephemeral: true , through the same state machine as other replies: If nothing was acknowledged, it is the reply. If the interaction was deferred publicly, the deferral is deleted and the view is an ephemeral follow-up. If a reply was already sent, the view is an ephemeral follow-up. Layouts do not apply to error views. Every error is logged with the route kind, id and file, whether or not a view runs.

heading: When the view fails
text: If the view itself throws, neocord logs that error too and sends the built-in message. Keep views simple. Error views are rendered once and are not live, so onClick and onSelect do not work in them. A button in an error view has to use route or customId .

heading: React error boundaries

A class component with componentDidCatch inside your tree also works, because @teamneo/neocord-react is a real React renderer. A loading.tsx file gives a slow command a visible placeholder. Its UI is sent as the reply right away, and the handler's result replaces it. The handler's result then replaces it in the same message: you used /report / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 12 new members joined this week.

heading: What it applies to

heading: How it works

Discord fixes visibility at the first response, so keep them consistent: A public placeholder with an ephemeral result: neocord deletes the placeholder and sends the result as an ephemeral follow-up. heading: Modals

Remove loading.tsx from this route or show the modal before any reply or slow work." A src/loading.tsx at the root applies to every command in the bot, so it rules out any command that opens a modal. Modals opened from a button are not affected, because buttons ignore loading .

heading: loading compared to autoDefer

With a loading file, the interaction is already acknowledged, so autoDefer does nothing. Use autoDefer alone unless you want control over what the placeholder says.

src/context.ts creates the services your handlers share, such as a database client. Its value is available as ctx.app in every handler, event and task, with its type generated from the file.

heading: defineContext
text: defineContext(factory) takes a function that may be async. The factory receives ContextFactoryArgs and returns a ContextResult . Argument Type Meaning client Client<true> The discord.js client. heading: Lifecycle
text: startBot handles the context in this order: Validates the manifest and creates the client. Runs the factory, and waits for it. Creates the dispatcher and wires events and tasks. Logs in. If the factory throws, the bot stops with "src/context.ts failed to create the app context: reason". On SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP or a shutdown request, startBot stops taking new interactions and events, waits up to five seconds for running tasks and handlers, expires live sessions, calls dispose , and then destroys the client. So a handler in the middle of an await can still use ctx.app , unless it outlasts that wait. An error from dispose is logged and does not stop the rest of the shutdown.

heading: One per process
text: The factory runs once in each shard process. With four shards you have four database pools, so size pools for that. The manager process does not create the context. See Sharding .

heading: Keep setup in the factory
text: neocord deploy , neocord build and neocord test import your route modules and src/context.ts to read command definitions, but they do not call the factory. Those commands can run with no real secrets, because they may set SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION . So open connections inside the factory and not at the top level of the module, as the template does with createDatabase() .

@teamneo/neocord-react is a React renderer built on react-reconciler , in the same way react-dom renders to the browser. Your components render to a tree of host elements, and that tree is serialised to Discord's Components V2 JSON and checked against Discord's limits. you used /welcome / my-bot APP Today at 12:00 Welcome Hello Ada , glad you are here. Get started Docs

heading: How the renderer works
text: React renders your function components. Hooks, context and <Suspense> work as they do anywhere else. The committed tree contains only host elements, which the components from @teamneo/neocord-react produce. The serialiser walks that tree. It collapses text, resolves custom ids, collects binary attachments, and validates each component. The result is a RenderResult that discord.js accepts directly. In a neocord handler you do not touch RenderResult . You return a node, and the runtime renders it. Outside neocord, see using it standalone .

heading: Why there are no embeds
text: Every message is sent with the IsComponentsV2 flag. Discord does not allow content or embeds on those messages, and in exchange the whole message is made of components. A Container with an accent colour takes the place of an embed, and it can hold text, images, files, sections and buttons in any order. @teamneo/neocord-react has no embed component. The no-embed-builders rule warns when a project uses EmbedBuilder or other discord.js builders.

heading: Limits
text: Each limit is enforced at render time, and the error names the component. A message can hold 40 components in total. Every TextDisplay , button, select, section, thumbnail and row counts, including ones nested in a Container , and also including text displays created by collapsed text. MediaItem and Option do not count. The id and customId values in a message must be unique. Each component page lists its own limits. Mentions are off by default in a bot: neocord sets allowedMentions: { parse: [] } on the client, so user input cannot ping anyone. Change it per message with Message , or for the whole bot through client in neocord.config.ts .

heading: Rendering in neocord

heading: How a click is handled
text: neocord renders your node through a live root. If the committed tree has any handler, the session is stored. Each live component gets a custom id of the form ~<sessionId>:<index> . The ~ prefix is reserved, so your own custom ids cannot start with it. A click re-checks the route that opened the session, as the warning below describes, then dispatches to the handler for that id. It waits for an async handler to finish. If the handler did not acknowledge the interaction, neocord updates the message with the latest render. text: The handler receives the discord.js interaction. You can read from it, or respond through it, and neocord then edits the message without responding again. A slow handler can outlast autoDefer , which acknowledges the click for you. The event's response methods keep working when that happens, so the same handler works however long it takes: Call after the automatic defer What neocord does event.reply(options) Sends it as a follow-up, which resolves to a Message . An ephemeral flag still applies. event.update(options) Edits the message with editReply . event.deferUpdate() Nothing, because the click is already acknowledged. event.deferReply(options) Nothing yet. heading: Updates outside a click
text: A state change from anything else also edits the message, such as a timer or a promise. Edits are coalesced: one edit runs at a time, and only the newest pending payload is sent. Intermediate states can be skipped under load. Discord rate limits still apply, so do not update more often than you need. A tree needs at least one handler for a session to exist, and without one it is unmounted right after sending.

heading: Replacing the message
text: A message shows one thing at a time, so a new delivery to the message ends the session on it. The tree unmounts, its effect cleanups run, and neither a timer nor the TTL can edit the message again. What replaces the message Example Editing the reply through the same ctx await ctx.reply(<Confirm />) , then await ctx.editReply(<Banned />) . A route button or select that updates A route button in the same tree that returns a node. A modal with respond: "update" opened from the message submit returns a node. Deleting the reply await ctx.deleteReply() . A follow-up, or a route with respond: "reply" , sends a new message and leaves the session running. So does a route that returns nothing. A respo

heading: TTL
text: A session has an idle timeout, set by live.ttl . Fact Detail Default 14m Accepted values A duration string, such as "5m" or "1h30m" , or a number of milliseconds, from 1ms to 2147483647ms (about 24.8 days). Anything else is a validateManifest error, which also fails startup. What resets it Each click on the session. A timer calling setState does not. When it passes The message is edited one last time with every button and select disabled, then the tree unmounts and effect cleanups run. The default sits under Discord's 15 minute lifetime for interaction tokens, which is what neocord edits through. The initial token is replaced by each click's, unless the handler answered that click with a rep

heading: Per-process limits
text: Sessions live in a Map in the process that created them. They are not persisted or shared. There is no database or Redis option. With sharding , each shard has its own store. Discord sends a guild's interactions to the shard that owns the guild, so clicks reach the shard holding the session, as long as the shard count does not change. Each open session keeps a React tree and its closures in memory until it expires. neocord sets no limit on the number of sessions, so a command that many people run all day can hold many trees. Lower live.ttl if that matters.

heading: Restart behaviour
text: Event Result Graceful stop (SIGINT, SIGTERM, manager shutdown) neocord tries to expire every session, so their components are disabled. It waits up to two seconds for those edits, then unmounts the rest. Crash or kill Nothing runs, so messages keep their enabled buttons. A click after either The session is gone, so neocord removes the live components from the message and sends an ephemeral "This message has expired." notice. Route buttons, route selects and link buttons stay, and rows or containers left empty are removed. If that would leave the message empty, only the notice is sent. The handler code does not run again. A shard is one gateway connection that handles a slice of your bot's servers. Discord requires sharding once a bot is in 2,500 or more servers, and if a bot needs it and does not have it, the gateway closes with code 4011. neocord always runs production bots through a sharding manager, so you do not change any code when you start needing more than one shard.

heading: How it works

Each shard runs one copy, with its own client, app context, dispatcher and tasks. deploy.js Calls deployCommands . See Deploying commands . neocord start launches manager.js . The manager wraps discord.js ShardingManager , applies your sharding config, spawns shard.js once per shard, logs each shard's lifecycle, respawns shards with a backoff, and forwards SIGINT , SIGTERM and SIGHUP . The manager never deploys commands, because it has no manifest and must not load route modules. Under deploy.mode: "auto" , neocord

heading: What each shard keeps to itself
text: Each shard has its own memory unless you use ctx.shards or an external store. Keep this in mind when you go from one shard to several: Cooldowns are in memory, per user and route, in each dispatcher. Live sessions live in the process that created them. See Live sessions . App context from src/context.ts is created once per shard, so each shard opens its own database connection or pool. Caches on ctx.client only hold the servers that shard handles. Tasks default to shard: "first" , which runs them only where the shard ids include 0 . Use shard: "all" for per-shard work. See Tasks .

heading: Stopping
text: When the manager receives SIGINT , SIGTERM , SIGHUP or a shutdown message , it cancels pending respawns, asks each shard to shut down, waits up to twelve seconds for each one, then kills any that are still running. A shard needs at most ten seconds, as its shutdown steps show, and the constants live together so the two cannot drift apart. Logs from a shard are prefixed with its id, and the manager logs under a manager scope. Set NEOCORD_LOG_LEVEL to override logLevel .

heading: Scaling advice
text: Leave totalShards on "auto" unless you have a reason to pin it. Pin it when you split shards across machines, because every manager must agree on the total. Do not lower spawnDelay to start faster. Discord rate limits gateway identifies, and the default leaves a gap between shards. Raise spawnTimeout if shards fail with ShardingReadyTimeout on a slow network, or if your src/context.ts takes a long time to connect. To run shards on more than one machine, set the same numeric totalShards everywhere and give each machine its own shardList . ctx.shards only reaches shards under the same manager, and shard: "first" tasks only run on the machine that hosts shard 0. heading: Why

heading: Why
text: A failed reply that nobody awaits is an unhandled rejection rather than an error your error view can show. It also lets the handler finish before the reply is sent. heading: Why
text: Without its own error.tsx , a feature falls back to the nearest one above it, or to a built-in message. Turn this on if each feature should explain its own failures. It is reported once per feature, on feature.ts or the feature's first file, and only an error.tsx at the feature root counts.

heading: Build and validate

Build the production bundle. neocord build validates routes and command payloads too, unless you pass --no-validate . Pass --typecheck to run tsc --noEmit first.

text: Run exactly one copy of each shard per token, and stop your local neocord dev before it connects to the same application as production. Two processes can both receive an interaction and race to answer it. Use a host that keeps a long-running process alive. See Hosting notes . Use Docker or a process manager , and give shutdowns enough time. Each shard gets up to twelve seconds to stop. Include your database migration step in your release process if you have one. See Drizzle or Prisma .

They stop working if you rename the file. See Upgrading .

Bundles keep packages external, so the runtime stage copies all of /app , including node_modules . @teamneo/neocord-cli is a dev dependency of the project, and start needs it, so dev dependencies are kept in the image. The container runs as the unprivileged bun user, and owns /app , because neocord start writes its bundled config to .neocord/cache and neocord deploy writes .neocord/deploy.json .

heading: Stopping
text: docker stop sends SIGTERM to the container's main process. When the signal reaches neocord, each shard waits for running tasks and handlers, expires live sessions, disposes the app context and destroys the client, and the manager gives each shard up to twelve seconds. See Process managers . Docker's default grace period of ten seconds is shorter than that, so a shard with slow work can be killed before dispose runs. Raise it with docker stop --time 20 , or stop_grace_period: 20s in Compose.

neocord manages its own shards, including respawning them after a crash with a growing delay, but it does not restart itself if the manager process exits or the machine reboots. Use a process manager for that.

heading: What neocord does on a signal
text: The CLI forwards SIGINT , SIGTERM and SIGHUP to the process it launched. Under neocord start , that process is the sharding manager. When the manager receives SIGINT , SIGTERM or SIGHUP : It logs Received <signal>, stopping shards. and cancels pending respawns. It asks each shard to shut down, and waits up to twelve seconds for each one. It kills any shard still running, then exits with code 0. Each shard shuts down in this order: Stop taking new interactions and events. Wait for running tasks and running handlers, up to five seconds. These run at the same time, so a slow handler gets to acknowledge its click and still has a working ctx.app . Expire live sessions, spending up to two seconds

heading: Exit codes and restart loops
text: neocord start exits with the manager's exit code. Exit code Meaning 0 A requested stop finished. 1 Startup failed, after logging one error with no stack trace. Or the bot was running and no shards are left to run. See Failure behaviour . / Warning A bad token does not loop inside neocord: a shard that reports one is not respawned. A process manager that restarts the whole command undoes that protection. Always set a restart delay and a limit, as in the examples below.

heading: systemd
text: The working directory must contain neocord.config.ts and the output of neocord build . The CLI loads .env files from the project root, or you can use EnvironmentFile . Then enable and start it: Replace /usr/local/bin/bun with the path from which bun . With Node, use ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm run start .

heading: pm2
text: Run the bot with one instance in fork mode. Do not use cluster mode or more than one instance, because each copy would start its own manager and connect the same shards. The file must end in .cjs because a neocord project sets "type": "module" .

heading: Windows
text: Windows has no POSIX signals. Pressing Ctrl+C in a console sends the event to the whole console, so the CLI waits up to twenty seconds for the child to stop by itself before it forwards SIGINT . Other ways of ending the process may skip the shutdown steps above.

heading: Logs
text: neocord writes debug and info to stdout, and warn and error to stderr, with an ISO timestamp on each line. Tokens are redacted. It does not write log files, so use your process manager's log handling. Set the level with logLevel in the config or NEOCORD_LOG_LEVEL in the environment, which takes priority. The levels are debug , info , warn , error and silent .

A neocord bot connects out to Discord's gateway over a WebSocket and stays connected. That decides what kind of hosting it needs.

heading: What the host must provide
text: Requirement Why A process that stays running The gateway connection, tasks and live sessions all live in memory. Outbound access to Discord The bot opens a WebSocket to the gateway and calls the REST API over HTTPS. Bun, or Node 22.22 or later @teamneo/neocord-cli declares node >=22.22.0 , and neocord start is how a bot runs. The runtime packages declare node >=22.12.0 . Environment variables At least DISCORD_TOKEN . See Environment variables . The bot does not need any of these: An inbound port. Interactions arrive over the gateway. neocord does not start an HTTP server, and has no HTTP interactions endpoint. A public domain or TLS certificate. Persistent disk , unless you use SQLite or wan

heading: Choosing a host
text: A VPS or dedicated server fits well, with Docker or a process manager . A container platform fits if it can run a background worker. Look for a service type that does not expect an open port, because neocord does not listen on one. A platform that restarts or stops a service for failing a port or HTTP health check will not work. Serverless functions do not fit. They cannot hold a gateway connection.

heading: Run one copy
text: Run one copy of each shard for each bot token. If you scale a service to several replicas, each one starts its own manager and connects the same shards, and Discord then delivers interactions to more than one of them. Handlers race, and you see code 40060 in the logs. To scale out, follow Sharding , and give each machine its own shardList . During a rolling deploy, the old and new versions can overlap and cause the same race for a moment. Stop the old copy first if that matters.

heading: Memory and CPU
text: process sharding runs each shard in its own process, so memory grows with the shard count. discord.js caches also grow with the number of servers. Measure your own bot, because the numbers depend on your intents and caches. To reduce cache use, pass the discord.js options through client in your config, and request only the intents you need. Avoid synchronous work in handlers, because it blocks the event loop and stops the autoDefer timer. The no-blocking-calls rule catches the common cases.

heading: Filesystem
text: neocord build writes to .neocord/build , and neocord start reads from it. Build the bot during your image or release step. .neocord must stay writable when the bot runs, even if nothing else is. neocord start bundles your config to .neocord/cache each time it launches, and a deploy writes .neocord/deploy.json .

heading: Time and networking
text: Discord's three second limit on acknowledging an interaction is measured from when Discord sends it, so slow networks reduce your margin. autoDefer runs at 2000 ms by default, and you can lower it with autoDefer: { after: 1000 } . A shard must connect within sharding.spawnTimeout , which defaults to 30 seconds. Raise it on a slow network. If Could not reach Discord appears in the logs, check your connection and Discord's status page .
Upgrade the neocord packages together, then run the same checks you use before a release.

heading: Update the packages
text: Leave out @teamneo/neocord-eslint-plugin if the project does not use ESLint. @teamneo/neocord-routing comes in as a dependency, so you do not need to list it. Check the peer dependencies at the same time: Package Peer dependency neocord , @teamneo/neocord-react discord.js ^14.28.0 , react ^19.3.0 @teamneo/neocord-cli neocord @teamneo/neocord-eslint-plugin eslint ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 Print the versions you ended up with: neocord info shows the installed versions, the runtime, the OS, and whether DISCORD_TOKEN is set, without printing its value. Include its output in bug reports.

heading: Check the project
text: Skip run lint if the project does not use ESLint. neocord typegen regenerates .neocord , and the typecheck script runs it first. You never edit that folder, and it is not committed, so there is nothing to migrate in it. neocord test validates every route and command payload, so it catches a definition the new version rejects. The dry run shows the commands you would send, including its hash. If the hash differs from the last deploy, the serialized commands changed, and you need to deploy.

heading: Things that can break in-flight messages
text: Discord keeps old messages and their components, so keep these in mind whenever you release a change, not only during upgrades. Renaming or moving a button, select or modal file changes its custom id. Clicking a component on an old message then shows This interaction is no longer available. and logs No route matches ... . Keep the old route for a while if the old messages matter. Changing a route's params breaks old custom ids in the same way. Changing a select's type makes old messages fail too, because the route expects another type. Live sessions do not survive a restart. Clicking an old button shows This message has expired. and removes its components.

heading: TypeScript
text: Generated projects run native TypeScript 7 as tsc , side by side with TypeScript 6 under the typescript package name when ESLint is enabled, because typescript-eslint needs the TypeScript 6 API. Keep both aliases when you upgrade: See Manual setup and the TypeScript 7 and ESLint section of Troubleshooting.

heading: Node
text: @teamneo/neocord-cli requires Node 22.22 or later, and the runtime packages require Node 22.12 or later. If you run on Node, check your version and any Docker base image when you upgrade. On Bun, keep Bun current.

Most neocord errors say what to do. This page lists the common ones with their exact text, so you can search for what you see. If nothing here helps, include the output of neocord info in your report. It prints whether DISCORD_TOKEN is set, and never its value.

heading: Invalid or missing token
text: Discord refused the login. Reset the token in the Developer Portal and update it. If you just reset it, the old value no longer works anywhere. The same problem has its own wording at two other points: If there is no token at all, you see this: Check that the variable is in a file the CLI loads. The order is .env , .env.<mode> , .env.local , .env.<mode>.local , and the real environment always wins. .env.local is skipped in test mode. See the CLI reference .

heading: Environment validation failed
text: A variable in src/env.ts is missing or invalid, and the lines below this message name each one. Set it in the environment or a .env file. dev , start and a real deploy always validate. See Environment variables .

heading: Disallowed intents (4014)
text: GuildMembers , GuildPresences and MessageContent are privileged. Enable each one you request in the Developer Portal, or remove it from intents in neocord.config.ts and from any defineFeature({ intents }) . heading: A shard keeps respawning
text: A shard exited, and the manager is bringing it back with a growing delay, up to a minute. The lines around it say why, such as Could not reach Discord during a network outage, or an uncaught exception from your code. The delay resets once the shard has stayed ready for a minute. See Failure behaviour .

heading: An event never fires
text: Events need intents. neocord test , neocord build and startup warn when one is missing: messageCreate and messageUpdate also warn that message.content, embeds and attachments stay empty without the privileged MessageContent intent . See Events .

heading: The three second limit
text: Discord gives each interaction three seconds to be acknowledged. neocord defers automatically after 2000 ms if your handler has not responded, so slow handlers do not hit the limit. You can change that in the config: Auto defer can still miss the limit in these cases: autoDefer: false is set and the handler is slow. Something blocks the event loop, so the timer cannot fire. Synchronous file or process calls are the usual cause, and the no-blocking-calls rule catches them. The process is overloaded, or the network is very slow. Lower after . What an automatic defer does depends on the route. Commands get a deferred reply, which Discord shows as a thinking state. Buttons and selects get a defe

heading: Unknown interaction (10062)
text: The words after Could not change with the action, such as edit the reply , follow up or show the modal . Discord no longer accepts this interaction, usually because the three second limit passed before the first acknowledgement. See The three second limit . This is logged as a warning, and does not crash the handler.

heading: Already acknowledged (40060)
text: Something else responded first. The likely causes are: Two processes are using the same token. A common one is neocord dev running while production is up, or two replicas of a service. Each process receives the interaction and they race. Stop one. A handler called ctx.interaction.reply directly. neocord follows the raw interaction's state, but it cannot see a response that is still in flight, so the two can race. Use ctx.reply or return JSX. The no-direct-interaction-reply rule catches this. neocord recovers where it can. A first reply or update that fails this way is retried as an edit, and handlers do not crash. See Replying .

heading: showModal fails
text: A modal must be the first response. Either loading.tsx applies to the route, the handler did slow work and autoDefer ran, or the handler already replied. Call ctx.showModal first. A modal submit cannot open another modal, and showModal is not on the modal context for that reason. See Modals .

heading: A root loading.tsx breaks commands that open a modal
text: src/loading.tsx applies to every slash command and context menu command in the bot, because the closest loading file wins and the root is the fallback. neocord sends the loading reply before your handler runs, so the interaction is already acknowledged when the handler calls ctx.showModal . Buttons and selects ignore loading files, so a modal opened from a button is not affected. Move the file into a feature or a command folder that contains no command that opens a modal. See Loading UI .

heading: Nothing happened, or the warning about returning nothing
text: A command must return a node or call a reply method. Otherwise Discord shows that the application did not respond. Buttons and selects that return nothing are acknowledged with a deferred update, and modals acknowledge silently, so only commands get this warning. See Replying . If you registered the commands in one scope, they do not appear in the other. Wa

heading: Interaction is no longer available
text: Users see this when no route matches a command or custom id, and the log says No route matches ... . Usually you renamed or removed a route that an old message still uses, or the deployed commands are older than the running code. Deploy again if it is a command. See Upgrading .

heading: This message has expired
text: The live session that owned this button or select is gone. Sessions are in memory per process, so they end on restart, and they also end after the idle timeout, live.ttl , which defaults to 14m , or when a new delivery replaces the message. See Live sessions .

heading: Can I use embeds?
text: No. @teamneo/neocord-react renders Components V2 only, and every message it produces has the IsComponentsV2 flag. Discord does not allow embeds on those messages. Use Container , which has an accentColor , in place of an embed. See UI overview .

heading: Can I use discord.js directly?
text: Yes. ctx.client and ctx.interaction are the real discord.js objects. Use them to read data and to call any API you need. Respond through ctx rather than ctx.interaction , so the reply state stays correct.

heading: Why did @here not ping anyone?
text: allowedMentions defaults to { parse: [] } through the client options, so nothing is pinged unless you allow it. Use <Message allowedMentions={...}> for one message, or client.allowedMentions in the config for all of them.

heading: Can anyone click my buttons?
text: Yes. Anyone who can see the message can click. Check ctx.user.id in the handler, or interaction.user.id in a live onClick , if that matters. A route can also use permissions , which is enforced at runtime on buttons and selects.

heading: Can I respond to plain messages instead of slash commands?
text: Yes. Add events/messageCreate.ts with defineEvent , and enable GuildMessages and the privileged MessageContent intent. See Events .

heading: Does a button still work after a restart?
text: A button with route or customId does, because the handler is found by its custom id. A button with onClick does not, because its handler lived in memory.

heading: Do I need Bun?
text: No. Everything runs on Node too. neocord test is the one exception to check: it uses vitest if the project depends on it, and otherwise needs Bun, so on Node either install Bun or add vitest. See Testing .

heading: Which Node version do I need?
text: @teamneo/neocord-cli declares Node 22.22 or later. neocord , @teamneo/neocord-react , @teamneo/neocord-routing , @teamneo/neocord-eslint-plugin and create-neocord declare Node 22.12 or later.

heading: Why does ctx.guild have a type that includes null?
text: The handler may run in a DM. Set guildOnly: true on the route, and ctx.guild and ctx.member become non-null. The prefer-guild-only rule suggests this when it finds ctx.guild! .

heading: startBot
text: The entry for one process. In order, it: Validates the manifest, logs warnings and fails on errors. Resolves the token, then merges intents and partials from enabled features. Creates the client, with allowedMentions: { parse: [] } as a default that config.client can override. Creates the app context from src/context.ts . Wires interactions and events, and starts tasks on clientReady . Logs in, with a 120 second timeout, and installs handlers for SIGINT , SIGTERM , SIGHUP , the { neocord: "shutdown" } IPC message and unhandled rejections. stop() stops taking new interactions and events, waits up to five seconds for running tasks and handlers, expires live sessions, disposes the app context a

heading: startManager
text: The production entry. It wraps discord.js ShardingManager , applies config.sharding , logs lifecycle events, supervises respawns with a backoff, and forwards SIGINT , SIGTERM , SIGHUP and the { neocord: "shutdown" } IPC message. A startup failure behaves as it does in startBot . See Failure behaviour . The shard count comes from the shards argument, then NEOCORD_SHARD_COUNT , then sharding.totalShards , then "auto" . It does not deploy commands, because it has no manifest and must not load route modules. See Sharding .

heading: deployCommands

heading: serializeCommands

heading: Prompts
text: Prompts run when stdin and stdout are both terminals and --yes is not set. Without a terminal, or with --yes , nothing prompts and the defaults above apply. Any value given as a flag skips its prompt. The order is: Order Prompt Choices Initial value 1 Where should the project be created? A path my-neocord-bot 2 <dir> is not empty. Continue and overwrite files that have the same name? Yes or no, only for a non-empty directory No 3 Which database toolkit do you want? None, Drizzle, Prisma. None is left out if --dialect was given. None, or Drizzle if --dialect was given 4 Which database will you use? SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, only if a database is chosen SQLite 5 Add ESLint with the neocord ru

heading: Exit codes
text: Code When 0 The project was created, even if git could not be initialized. Also after --help or --version , and when you cancel a prompt, which prints Cancelled. Nothing was created. 1 Invalid flags or options, an unusable directory, or a failed dependency install. If the install fails, the project files stay in place and you can retry it yourself. Git problems are warnings and do not change the exit code: Situation Behaviour The target is already inside a repository Skips git init. git is missing, or init fails Warns that it could not initialize git.
